sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusables and KG hints, Safe driving practices

FACT_ID: sec15-R01 | anchor: A01
The long-trip rest rule is a ten-minute break at least every two hours, and the break counts only when spent outside the vehicle [A01].
Why it matters: group fatigue; difficulty medium; prereq sec15-F04; confusables sec15-F03, sec15-F04 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec15-R02 | anchor: A01
Metropolitan rush hour runs inbound from seven to nine in the morning but outbound from four to six in the afternoon [A01].
Why it matters: group traffic-conditions; difficulty medium; prereq sec15-F06; confusables sec15-F06, sec15-F07 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec15-R03 | anchor: A03
The only legal safety belt exception is a person eighteen or older in the back seat, while a child under eight needs a child safety device unless the child is at least four feet nine inches tall [A03].
Why it matters: group belts-and-seats; difficulty high; prereq sec15-F16; confusables sec15-F16, sec15-F19 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec15-R04 | anchor: A03
Wearing safety belts cuts the risk of collision injury or death by forty-five to fifty percent, and the lap belt should fit snugly and comfortably across the lower hips [A03].
Why it matters: group belts-and-seats; difficulty medium; prereq sec15-F17; confusables sec15-F17, sec15-F18 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec15-R05 | anchor: A04
With anti-lock brakes you press hard and keep steering, because pumping, the old advice for ordinary brakes, can cost all braking force in an anti-lock vehicle [A04].
Why it matters: group anti-lock-brakes; difficulty high; prereq sec15-F21; confusables sec15-F21, sec15-F22 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec15-R06 | anchor: A04
Anti-lock brakes shorten a sudden stop by only about ten percent at best, so their real benefit is steering control rather than stopping distance [A04].
Why it matters: group anti-lock-brakes; difficulty medium; prereq sec15-F22; confusables sec15-F21, sec15-F22 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec15-R07 | anchor: A04
A rear-facing infant seat never goes in front of a passenger air bag, and children twelve and under belong buckled in the rear seat [A04].
Why it matters: group air-bags; difficulty high; prereq sec15-F25; confusables sec15-F19, sec15-F25 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec15-R08 | anchor: A04
Around an air bag the hands sit at four and eight o'clock on the wheel, and most people killed by air bags were not wearing seat belts [A04].
Why it matters: group air-bags; difficulty medium; prereq sec15-F24; confusables sec15-F23, sec15-F24 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec15-R09 | anchor: A02
When another vehicle passes you, slow down and keep right rather than treating it as a challenge, and when you pass, exceeding the speed limit is illegal [A02].
Why it matters: group passing; difficulty medium; prereq sec15-F13; confusables sec15-F13, sec15-F14 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec15-R10 | anchor: A03
In the ten passing steps the warning to the other driver comes by horn or flashing lights, and the merge back right waits until the passed vehicle's headlights show in your rear view mirror [A03].
Why it matters: group passing; difficulty medium; prereq sec15-F15; confusables sec15-F15 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec15-R11 | anchor: A04
An adjustable head restraint fits against the back of the head, not the neck, because its job is to limit whiplash in a rear-end collision [A04].
Why it matters: group safety-equipment; difficulty low; prereq sec15-F20; confusables sec15-F20 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0078]
